status_source: confirmed: hinges, lock and pull are HOLD envelopes of reserved space on the glass until a rated set is named (D-46, D-56); no holes or cut-outs in the glass until then (PM ruling on the FRONT plan)

status_source: confirmed: D-104 (2026-11-01): a CAD body whose name carries ENVELOPE stands in for unnamed or HOLD hardware until the maker's model goes in; the first case is the door strike 368102
why: the stand-in takes the space the part will take, so its overlap with the part it clamps is expected; only for hardware (a bought number, xx8000 to xx8999, with ENVELOPE in the same name) and only within its own assembly file, so a skeleton panel envelope or a clash with another team's part still counts

status_source: calculation: the base keys' M6 holes are tapped (joints register J-BASE-02, D-95); a screw modelled at its 6.0 mm size overlaps a thread modelled at the 5.0 mm drill by 8.64 mm3 per mm of engagement (90.7 for the fixing screws' 10.5 mm, 122.7 for the hook studs' 14.2 mm, measured in Fusion on main 97a1aeb); 260 allows up to 30 mm
why: a screw in its own tapped hole is the joint, not a clash; more than a thread's overlap still counts
